subject.title: [Bug] Orphaned/oversized native Codex thread wedges a session permanently — chat.send returns started but no run executes, silently dropping messages

question: What liveness contract should WebChat/Codex enforce when a native Codex thread cannot reliably start a turn for an accepted `chat.send`?
rationale: The source points to a real post-ACK liveness gap, but choosing fail-fast, forced rotation, or recovery/audit behavior changes user-visible semantics and needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Force-rotate unsafe native threads before ACK
options.body: Treat suspect or oversized Codex native bindings as unhealthy before `chat.send` returns `started`, then start the user turn on a fresh thread when possible.

options.title: Fail fast before ACK
options.body: Return a visible send failure instead of `started` whenever Codex startup cannot prove the turn can be scheduled promptly.

options.title: Add recovery/audit first
options.body: Keep the current ACK behavior but add a health/audit path that detects accepted not-started runs and recovers or surfaces them to users.

recommendation.title: Force-rotate unsafe native threads before ACK
recommendation.body: Treat suspect or oversized Codex native bindings as unhealthy before `chat.send` returns `started`, then start the user turn on a fresh thread when possible.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the adjacent Codex budget guard that is closest to the force-rotate option and native-thread health boundary.
